questions.question: As of March 2023, how many High Courts are there in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __25.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• High Courts:-

 
 
• ​The institution of the high court originated in India in 1862 with three high courts set up at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.
 
• The fourth HC was established in Allahabad in 1866.
 
• Currently, India has a total of 25 High Courts established in different states of the country.
 
• The Andhra Pradesh High Court became the** 25th** High Court of India when it was established on **January 1, 2019.** 
 
• The UTs of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh have a common high court.
 
• Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the organisation, independence, jurisdiction, powers, procedures and so on of the HC.
 
• The Seventh Amendment Act of 1956 authorised the Parliament to establish a common HC for two or more states or two or more states and a UT
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Jurisdiction of High Courts

 
 
• Bombay HC - Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu
 
• Guwahati HC - Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh
 
• Punjab and Haryana HC - Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh
 
• Calcutta HC - West Bengal, Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.question: Which species is known as black lipped pearl oyster found in the Indo-Pacific, within tropical coral reefs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pinctada margaritiferau**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pinctada margaritifera**, commonly known as the **black-lipped pearl oyster**, is a bivalve mollusc belonging to the family **Pteriidae**
 
• It is **widely distributed in the Indo-Pacific region, particularly within tropical coral reef ecosystems.**
 
• These **environments provide the optimal conditions for its survival, including warm water temperatures and an abundance of plankton for food.**
 
• The term **"black-lipped" refers to the distinct dark colouration found on the inner edges of its shell.**
 
• This **feature distinguishes it from other pearl oysters.**
 
• This species is particularly valued in the pearl industry as it is a primary producer of high-quality Tahitian black pearls, which are renowned for their unique colours and lustre.
 
• Like** other bivalves, it filters water for food, contributing to the clarity and health of its marine environment.**
 
• It also serves as a habitat for various small marine organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aplysia dactylomela:**

 
 
• Also known as the spotted sea hare, it is a sea slug.
 
• These animals are known for their soft, wrinkled bodies, which can have various colours and patterns, including spots.
 
• They **have a distinct head region with tentacles, and their bodies are somewhat flattened.**
 
 
 
• **Dentalium neohexagonum:**
 
 
• **A species of scaphopod mollusk, also known as a tusk shell**
 
• Scaphopods are marine molluscs that have tubular, tapered shells that are open at both ends.
 
• **These shells resemble the shape of an elephant’s tusk, which is how they got the name "tusk shell."**
 
 
 
• **Chatepleura apiculata:**
 
 
• **A type of chiton, which is a class of mollumolluscs **that cling to rocks in intertidal zones
 
• *Chatepleura apiculata* is a small, e**longated gastropod with a conical, smooth shell,** although its size and appearance can vary depending on its environment and the host it attaches to.

questions.question: The CSO adopted the concept of Gross Value Added in _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**January 2015**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Central Statistics Office (CSO)** adopted the concept of **Gross Value Added (GVA)** in **January 2015** as part of a major revision in the national accounts statistics.
 
• This change was implemented when the base year for GDP calculation was shifted from **2004-05 to 2011-12**.
 
• GVA measures the contribution of each sector to the economy.
 
• It reflects the value of goods and services produced in an economy after deducting the cost of inputs and raw materials.
 
• This adoption aligns India's statistical calculations with international practices and standards like those recommended by the **United Nations System of National Accounts (SNA)**.
 
• Along with the introduction of GVA, the **base year revision to 2011-12** was applied to GDP estimates.
 
• This revision ensured more accurate and updated data representation, helping policymakers assess economic performance better.

questions.question: Which of the following social reformers of 19th century India was the author of 'Stree Purush Tulana'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tarabai Shinde**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tarabai Shinde (1850–1910) wrote Stree Purush Tulana**, or A Comparison Between Women and Men, in 1882.
 
• **Shinde was a feminist activist who protested against caste and patriarchy in 19th-century India.** 
 
• Stree Purush Tulana is **considered one of the first modern feminist texts in India.**
 
• The book critiques the gender and caste systems and questions the position of women in society and their rights.
 
• **It was controversial for its time because it challenged Hindu religious scriptures as a source of women's oppression. **
 
• Shinde was born in the Berar province of Buldhana in modern-day Maharashtra.
 
• She was a member of the Satyashodhak Samaj and an associate of Savitribai Phule and Jyotirao Phule

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swarnakumari Devi**

 
 
• A prominent **Bengali writer, social reformer, and the first woman to edit a literary magazine in India.**
 
• She **was the daughter of Debendranath Tagore and the sister of Rabindranath Tagore.**
 
• Her work advocated for women's education and empowerment during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
 
 
• **Pandita Ramabai**
 
 
• A **social reformer and educationist who worked extensively for women's rights and education, especially for widows in India.**
 
• She** founded the Arya Mahila Samaj and the Mukti Mission for destitute women.**
 
• She was **one of the earliest proponents of women's education in colonial India and a pioneering feminist figure.**
 
 
 
• ** Usha Mehta**
 
 
• A prominent freedom fighter and Gandhian.
 
• **Famous for running the Congress Radio, an underground radio station, during the Quit India Movement (1942) to broadcast messages against British rule.**

questions.question: Which physical feature of India prevents the cold winds from central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinents?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Himalayas**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himalayas are the physical feature that prevents cold winds from Central Asia from entering the Indian subcontinent**
 
• The **Himalayas are a lofty mountain range that blocks cold winds from Central Asia from entering India.**
 
• The Himalayas' height, location, and complex topography significantly impact the climate of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The **Himalayas also influence the monsoons, forcing the rain-bearing winds to lose most of their moisture before crossing the range. **
 
• The Himalayas cause the Indian subcontinent to experience milder winters than Central Asia.
 
• **Northern India also has higher temperatures than other areas on the same latitudes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian plain**s

 
 
• **The Northern Plains, also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain**, are the granaries of India and the foundation for early civilizations.
 
• This vast plain is formed by the **rivers Ganga**, **Yamuna**, **Brahmaputra**, and their tributaries.
 
• It stretches across northern and northeastern India, covering states like **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, **West Bengal**, **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The Indo-Gangetic plain is characterized by fertile soils, making it one of the most important agricultural regions in India.
 
• It is densely populated, with major cities like **Delhi**, **Kolkata**, **Lucknow**, and **Patna** located along its course.
 
 
 
• **Indian desert**
 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is India's largest desert, covering about 77,000 square miles.
 
• The Thar Desert spans across parts of **Rajasthan**, **Gujarat**, **Punjab**, and **Haryana** in India, extending into **Pakistan**.
 
• It covers around **200,000 square kilometres** in India, primarily in the state of Rajasthan.
 
• The desert supports sparse vegetation like **cactus**, **acacia trees**, and **scrub plants**.
 
 
 
• **Coastal area**s
 
 
• **India's coastal areas include the coastal states of Gujarat**, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal, as well as the coastal union territories of Daman & Diu, Puducherry, Lakshadweep Islands, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
 
• **Coastal plains are low-lying**, flat areas of land that are adjacent to the sea or ocean.
 
• The elevation of the land increases gradually from the sea to the highlands. 
 
• **India's other main physical features include the Himalayas and the Peninsular Plateau.**

questions.question: Which state initiated the implementation of the Mid-day Meal scheme in elementary schools?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Mid Day Meal Scheme

 
 
• ​​Tamil Nadu was the first state in India to introduce this scheme.
 
• The first school which had the scheme since 1925 was Sourashtra Boys Higher Secondary School, Madurai.
 
• K. Kamaraj, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu at the time, introduced it first in Chennai and later extended it to all districts of Tamil Nadu.
 
• On 28th November 2001, the Supreme Court asked all state governments to begin this programme in their schools within 6 months.
 
 
 
• Nutritious Mid-day Meal scheme
 
 
• ​Nutritious Meal Programme was introduced by the then Chief Minister Puratchi Thalaivar Dr M.G.R. on 01.07.1982.
 
• The main objective of the programme is to emphasize education along with nutrition.
 
• Under this programme free hot cooked nutritious meal is being provided to children in Government Schools, Government aided Schools, Special Training Centres Madarasas, Maktabs supported under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and also in Special Schools functioning under National Child Labour Programme.
 
 

83:T

questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters of India is the author of the book, ‘The Indian Struggle’?

The correct answer is __**Subhas Chandra Bose**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subhas Chandra Bose is the author of The Indian Struggle**, a two-part book that covers the history of the Indian independence movement from 1920–1942:
 
• T**he Indian Struggle, 1920–1934: **
 
 
• **The first part of the book, published in 1948** after India gained independence
 
 
 
• **The Indian Struggle, 1935–1942:**
 
 
• **The second part of the book** 
 
 
 
• 11 Freedom Fighters of India Who Shaped the Nation's Destiny
 
• **The British colonial government banned the book in India. **
 
• Bose was a revolutionary leader who founded the Indian National Army (INA).
 
• He **also gave the slogan "Dilli Chalo" to motivate the INA in 1944. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi (1869–1948**)

 
 
• **Known as the Father of the Nation**, he led India’s struggle for independence through non-violent civil disobedience.
 
• **Key movements:**
 
 
• Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Salt Satyagraha (1930), and the Quit India Movement (1942).
 
 
 
• **Advocated for truth (Satya) and non-violence (Ahimsa) as core principles.**
 
 
 
• **Motilal Nehru (1861–1931)**
 
 
• A **prominent lawyer, freedom fighter**, and senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• He** was the father of Jawaharlal Nehru, India’s first Prime Minister.**
 
• Played a k**ey role in drafting the Nehru Report (1928)**, which was a response to the Simon Commission, proposing a constitution for India.
 
 
 
• **Vallabhbhai Patel (1875–1950)**
 
 
• **Known as the Iron Man of India,** he played a pivotal role in India’s integration post-independence by unifying 562 princely states.
 
• A** staunch supporter of Mahatma Gandhi, he was deeply involved in movements like the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) and the Quit India Movement (1942).**
 
• India’s **first Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Home Affairs.**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions about the organisation of 'Village Panchayats'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 40**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 40 of the Indian Constitution mentions the organization of village panchayats**
 
• Article 40 of the Constitution **states that the state shall take steps to organize village panchayats and give them the powers and authority to function as units of self-government. **
 
• Article 40 is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for framing laws and policies.
 
• **The DPSP is in Part IV of the Constitution, Articles 36–51. **
 
• **Panchayati raj**
 
 
• The Panchayati raj system is a system of local self-government for villages in rural India.
 
 
 
• **It includes the Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), which are responsible for**: 
 
 
• Economic development 
 
• Strengthening social justice 
 
• Implementing Central and State Government Schemes 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 36**

 
 
• This **article of the Statute of the International Court of Justice defines the Court's jurisdiction.**
 
• It **states that the Court's jurisdiction includes all cases** referred to it by the parties, as well as matters specified in the Charter of the United Nations, treaties, and conventions. 
 
 
 
• **Article 38**
 
 
• This **article of the Convention on the Rights of the Child covers a range of topics, including:**
 
 
• **Respecting international humanitarian law in armed conflicts **
 
• **Ensuring that children under 15 do not directly participate in hostilities **
 
• Protecting and caring for children affected by armed conflicts 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Articles 36**
 
 
• ​It states that the term **“State”** in this part (Part IV) has the same meaning as in **Part III** (which deals with Fundamental Rights).

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India grants power to the President to appoint Judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 124(2)**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 124(2) of the Constitution of India gives the President the power to appoint judges to the Supreme Court: **
 
• Th**e President appoints judges** by warrant under their hand and seal.
 
• The President consults with other Supreme Court judges and High Court judges in the states when appointing a judge.
 
• The **Chief Justice of India is always consulted when appointing a judge other than the Chief Justice.**
 
• Judges **serve until they turn 65 years old.**
 
• **Judges can resign by writing to the President. **
 
• **Article 124 **of the Constitution also covers the establishment and composition of the Supreme Court.
 
• It states that the Supreme Court is made up of the Chief Justice of India and up to seven other judges, as determined by Parliament

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 123*(1): Gives the President the power to issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session.**

 
 
• The **President can issue an ordinance if they believe immediate action is necessary.**
 
• The ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, but it must be laid before both houses of Parliament.
 
• The ordinance will stop working after six weeks from when Parliament reconvenes, or if both houses pass resolutions disapproving it before then.
 
• The President can also withdraw the ordinance at any time.
 
 
 
• **Article 127(3)**
 
 
• It Deals with the **appointment of an Ad hoc** **Chief Justice of India**.
 
• This provision comes into play when the **office of the Chief Justice of India** is vacant due to reasons like **resignation**, **death**, or **retirement**, and there is no provision for the **appointment of a new Chief Justice** at that time.
 
 
 
• **Article 128(4)**
 
 
• **Article 128(4)** of the Indian Constitution relates to the **attendance of retired judges** of the Supreme Court in the proceedings of the Supreme Court as **ad hoc judges**.
 
• **"A Judge of the Supreme Court who has ceased to hold office may, with his consent, be requested by the President to attend any sitting of the Supreme Court for the purpose of assisting the Court."**

questions.question: In which year was the International Olympic Committee formed?

• The **IOC** is the supreme authority of the Olympic Movement, overseeing the organization of the Summer and Winter Olympic Games.
 
• The Olympic Games are held every **four **years, alternating between Summer and Winter editions.
 
• The **IOC **is guided by the Olympic Charter, which outlines the principles and rules governing the Olympic Movement.
 
• The** IOC **works closely with** National Olympic Committees** (NOCs) from around the world to ensure the participation of athletes in the Olympic Games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Commonwealth Games are a multi-sport event involving athletes from **Commonwealth countries** and territories.
 
• The Asian Games are a multi-sport event involving athletes from **Asia**.

questions.question: To which group do the alkaline earth metals such as radium, barium and strontium belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 2A**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Alkaline earth metals like radium, barium, and strontium belong to group 2A (group 2) of the periodic table.
 
• The other elements in this group are beryllium and magnesium. 
 
• Alkaline earth metals are called group 2 elements because they have two valence electrons in their outer shell. 
 
• Some uses of alkaline earth metals include:
 
• Strontium: Used in fireworks to produce a crimson red color
 
• Barium: Used in rat poison as barium carbonate.

• Also known as the alkali metals or lithium family, these elements have one valence electron.
 
• They are very reactive metals that are soft and have a low density.

• Some examples of elements in this group include aluminum, gallium, indium, and thallium.

questions.question: Gautamiputra Satakarni titled Rajaraja and Maharaja is related to which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satavahana**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gautamiputra Satakarni was a ruler of the Satavahana dynasty** and was given the titles of Rajaraja and Maharaja.
 
• The **Satavahanas were an ancient Indian dynasty that ruled the Deccan region of India**, which is present-day Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Maharashtra. 
 
• ** The Satavahana dynasty and Gautamiputra Satakarni**:
 
 
• The **Satavahanas ruled after the Mauryan Empire declined. **
 
• The term "Satavahana" comes from the Prakrit word meaning "driven by seven". 
 
• The **Satavahanas were also known as the Andhras in the Puranas. **
 
• The Satavahana kingdom's capital cities included Amaravati, Pratishthana, and Kotalingala. 
 
• **Gautamiputra Satakarni ruled from 106 AD to 130 AD.** 
 
• He is **considered the greatest ruler of the Satavahana dynasty.** 
 
• He is believed to have restored the fortunes of the Satavahanas. 
 
• **He called himself the only Brahmana who defeated the Shakas. **
 
• His son was Vasisthiputra Sri Pulamavi/Pulumavi or Pulamavi II. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shunga Dynasty (Pataliputra)**

 
 
• The Shunga Dynasty was founded by Pushyamitra Shunga around 185 BCE after overthrowing the last Maurya ruler, Brihadratha.
 
• **Pushyamitra was a general in the Maurya Empire and took control after assassinating Brihadratha.**
 
• The dynasty played a significant role in reviving **Vedic religion** and **Brahmanical practices**, and its rulers are often credited with restoring temples and rituals dedicated to Hindu deities.
 
 
 
• **Pandya Dynasty (Madurai):**
 
 
• The **Pandya Dynasty was one of the oldest known dynasties i**n southern India and is mentioned in the Vedic texts.
 
• The P**andyas ruled primarily in the region of Tamil Nadu,** with their capital at Madurai.
 
• The **Pandyas were great patrons of Tamil culture, and their reign is often associated with the Sangam period,** during which Sangam literature flourished.
 
• This literature included epic poems, songs, and stories that celebrated Tamil kings, warriors, and the culture.
 
 
 
• **Shaka Dynasty (Ujjain, Mathura):**
 
 
• The Shaka dynasty **was founded by Central Asian Scythians (nomads), who migrated into India around the 2nd century BCE.**
 
• The Shakas established their rule primarily in the regions of Ujjain and Mathura.
 
• The **Shakas were skilled warriors and played a significant role in Indian military history**.
 
• They introduced the Shaka Era, a calendar system that was widely adopted by other Indian dynasties.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution contains Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article 51A.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points: __**In the Constitution of India, fundamental duties are mentioned in Article 51A.

 
• There was no list of fundamental duties in the original constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties were added into the Indian constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976.
 
• the 42nd constitutional amendment added Part IV A and Article 51A to the Indian constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties were added to the Indian constitution on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Initially, there were only 10 fundamental duties in the constitution.
 
• The 86th **Constitutional Amendment** Act 2002 added one more fundamental duty to the constitution.
 
• Currently, there are 11 fundamental duties in the Indian constitution.
 
• The idea of fundamental duties was borrowed from the Russian constitution.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-justiciable in nature.

The 11 Fundamental Duties listed are:

 
• Respect the National Flag, National Anthem, and the Indian Constitution's principles and institutions.
 
• Uphold and uphold the lofty principles that motivated the nation's fight for freedom.
 
• Uphold and defend India's sovereignty, unification, and integrity.
 
• Defend the nation and perform national service as required.
 
• Promote harmony and a feeling of shared brotherhood among all Indians, notwithstanding differences in religion, language, location, or section, and condemn behaviours that are demeaning to women's dignity.
 
• Appreciate and safeguard the rich cultural history of the nation as a whole.
 
• Maintaining a healthy ecosystem, including woods, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, as well as showing compassion for all living things.
 
• Foster a humanistic outlook, a scientific mindset, and a spirit of reformation
 
• Protect public property and abstain from violence
 
• Strive for excellence in all areas of personal and group endeavour so that the country continually reaches greater heights of endeavour and success.
 
• Give his kid or ward between the ages of six and fourteen the opportunity to pursue an education. The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002 added this duty.

questions.question: Mohiniyattam is associated with which of the following traditional dance styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lasva-style**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam is associated with the Lasya style of dance.**
 
• Mohiniyattam is a** classical solo dance form from Kerala, India, and is a subgenre of Lasya.**
 
• It is **performed in the Kaisiki vritti, **which is a graceful style of dance. 
 
• It is believed to have originated in the 16th century in Kerala's temples.
 
• The** name comes from the words "Mohini"** (meaning enchantress) and "attam" (meaning dance).
 
• **It is performed as a solo recital by women**.
 
• Dancers typically wear a white or off-white sari with gold borders, and their hair is adorned with jasmine flowers.
 
• It is characterized by graceful movements, swaying body, and subtle facial expressions.
 
• It is o**ne of the eight Indian classical dance forms recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samapadam (Equal Foot/Step):**

 
 
• The **term "Samapadam" refers to a balanced stance where weight** is evenly distributed on both feet, symbolizing stability and equilibrium.
 
• **In this posture, the dancer stands with their feet parallel, with both feet placed flat on the ground and equal pressure on each foot.**
 
• The **posture is commonly used in several classical dance forms like Bharatanatyam and Kathak to convey harmony, calmness, and balance.**
 
 
 
• **Tribhanga (Three Bends):**
 
 
• "**Tribhanga" literally means "three bends" in Sanskrit,** referring to the shape formed by bends at the neck, torso, and knee.
 
• This c**lassical pose, common in Bharatanatyam, Odissi, and other Indian dance forms**, creates an elegant S-shape with graceful curves.
 
• **The dancer's neck is tilted to one side, t**he torso is bent to the side, and the knee is slightly bent, creating a flowing, fluid form.
 
 
 
• **Chowk (Square, Strong Position):**
 
 
• **"Chowk" is a stance used in Kathak (and sometimes in other dance forms), symbolizing strength, stability, and a grounded posture.**
 
• In the **Chowk pose, the dancer stands with their feet wide apart and the body squared to the front.**
 
• The knees are bent deeply, and the upper body is often upright and strong.
 
• The position creates a square-like form, representing power and steadfastness.v
